name: Cyclic CA
miniText: How can cyclic local competition organize a disordered field into waves and spirals? NetLogo Cyclic CA assigns each patch a state on a color cycle. A patch advances only when enough neighbors occupy its successor state, using a selectable Moore or von Neumann neighborhood and radius. Fisch and colleagues [1] study threshold-range scaling in cyclic and excitable automata, Shalizi and Shalizi [2] examine how to quantify organization in cyclic systems, and Greenberg and Hastings [3] provide a related excitable-media comparison. The original model freezes states before updating to preserve simultaneous decisions. Threshold, state count, neighborhood geometry, and finite boundaries determine whether activity persists or freezes. Attractive spiral images illustrate local interaction and symmetry breaking; they do not by themselves quantify organization or establish a chemical, neural, or ecological explanation.
